traits.division_pattern.note: Wikipedia, Maple (read 2026-10-16): most maples have palmately veined leaves with three to nine lobes, one per main vein; a few are pinnately compound (box-elder) or pinnately veined. Stated here so maples do not take Sapindales' pinnate.

traits.wood_modulus_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, green: the range of the 5 Acer species it tests (bigleaf, black, red, silver, sugar), median typical. A species with its own row states its own.

traits.wood_rupture_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, green modulus of rupture: the range of the 5 Acer species it tests (bigleaf, black, red, silver, sugar), median typical. A species with its own row states its own.

traits.wood_moisture_green_share.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 4-1: average moisture of green heartwood and sapwood of the Acer species it lists (silver, sugar), as shares of oven-dry mass; the range, median typical.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 genus aggregate for Acer (gwddagg_v2.2_genus.csv, read): specific gravity 0.55 (wsg_est, the hierarchical-model genus mean, from 1015 records in 46 sources); trunks 0.55, branches 0.53. A species with its own measurements states its own. Basic density is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.note: Jepson's Manual of the Flowering Plants of California (1925), read in full, as Aceraceae: flowers regular, polygamous or dioecious; calyx generally 5-cleft; petals as many or none; stamens 3 to 10 on the edge of a disk; pistil 1 with a 2-lobed, 2-celled ovary and 2 styles, ripening a double samara. Jepson eFlora (as quoted in search results; the page itself was not read): stamens 5 to 12; genus summaries say mostly 8.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 219 Aceraceae (maples, which APG puts in Sapindaceae): trees or shrubs with scaled buds; leaves opposite, simple, palmately lobed or pinnate; fruit a two-winged samara whose halves separate.

traits.fruit_type.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 219 Aceraceae (maples, which APG puts in Sapindaceae): trees or shrubs with scaled buds; leaves opposite, simple, palmately lobed or pinnate; fruit a two-winged samara whose halves separate.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 362-364: maples' leaves are opposite (Sapindaceae subfamily Hippocastanoideae, with Aesculus), each pair crossing the one below, where most of the family's leaves are spiral.
